comment: Declared differences between BC's own metadata emitter and the runner's
SymbolReference-derived MetaTable. Issue #3533.
This file IS the allowlist: MetadataEquivalenceHarnessTests fails on any difference not
listed here, and equally on any entry here that no longer matches anything. So a reader
fix must delete its entries in the same change, and a BC version that introduces a new
property surfaces as a new undeclared difference rather than passing silently.
Every entry carries a reason AND exactly one KIND of reason, because the four kinds need
different evidence:
issue            a defect, tracked, expected to go away
outOfScope       the runner does not implement the surface, so no AL test can see it
(needs a Doc pointer)
oracleLimitation the ground truth is the wrong shape for this member, so the difference
says nothing about the runner (needs a Doc pointer)
cannotExpress    the symbol file cannot express it AND it cannot be derived
NO ENTRY CURRENTLY CLAIMS cannotExpress. Seven TranslationKey entries did, on the evidence
that SymbolReference.json stores no translation keys. That was true and the conclusion was
wrong twice over: the key is COMPUTED from names rather than stored (2,153 of 2,153
reproduced), and the runner reads no translation files anyway, so it is out of scope rather
than impossible. 'Nothing is stored' is evidence about storage, never about derivability.
Nine entries are DIRECTION-SCOPED. An entry covers both directions unless it says otherwise,
and a reason that justifies one direction must not license the other. All three
oracleLimitation entries are runner-only: they exist because the runner shows a merged
runtime view, so BC-absent / runner-present is what they justify — while the reverse, BC
emitting a field the runner never builds, is a hard reader defect that must still fail.
There is deliberately NO occurrence cap. One was implemented and used by nothing, which made
the PR claim a ratchet the code did not keep. No entry here has a bound that survives a
rebuild — the counts move with the BC build and with which apps are bundled — so any cap
would be a number nobody measured. Direction narrows categorically instead.
Measured on BC 28.1.49838.53910 over Business Foundation (12 tables) and System Application
(138 tables): 64,494 differences across 63 members. #3568 has removed twelve members so far.
Six were the KEY cluster -- 688 differences on MetaKey.KeyName / Clustered / Unique /
SumIndexFields, MetaKey.DebuggerDisplay and FieldMetadataRelation.Name, see
docs/metadata-equivalence.md#keys. Four more were the PLATFORM-FIELD cluster, 2,850
differences: MetaField.TestRelations (900) and MetaField.ValidateRelation (300) are now zero
and their entries are gone, while MetaField.AllowInCustomizations fell 755 -> 5 and
MetaField.ClrType 1,888 -> 988, both keeping an entry for their DECLARED-field half. The
runner appends BC's six platform fields itself and built them through MetaField's POSITIONAL
ctor, whose defaults differ from the XmlNode ctor BC's SystemFieldsHelper uses; it now copies
those four members off BC's own instance rather than restating them, so a BC version that
changes one moves both sides together. Per-member counts and examples are on issue #3568.
PageDefinition was added to the comparison by #3782 step 1, and the 117 entries below are the
result. Measured on BC 28.1.49838.53910 over Business Foundation and System Application (235
pages): 32,958 differences across 124 members.
READ THE 117 CAREFULLY: 49 of them are #field / *Specified COMPANION entries, which BC's own
serializer sets from the same value as the member declared beside them. So there are 68 DISTINCT
members, not 117, and comparing the raw count against the table side's overstates the page gap.
issue 3784  55 entries (30 distinct members). Properties SymbolReference.json already carries
and EmitPageXml does not read -- including the Actions (106 pages), Methods (107)
and Views (4) arrays. Extensible is the sharpest: the runner hardcodes "1", BC
answers 0 on 104 of 235 pages, and the symbol file states Extensible=0 for ALL 104
with zero omissions, so it is a pure read-don't-guess fix.
outOfScope  62 entries (38 distinct members). The ordinary field-control tree the runner does
not build today, plus the translation keys.
NONE of the outOfScope page entries claims a value is UNDERIVABLE, and that distinction is the
point. An earlier draft of this file said the control tree could not be proven faithful because
the symbol file stores AL text rather than the compiled DataColumnName. That was wrong, and it
would have recorded a live architecture question as settled: DataColumnName IS the field number,
control ids are identical in both sources, and 442 of 442 Rec-bound controls resolve exactly
against this harness's ground truth. ControlGUID is likewise a pure encoding of (page id,
control id) -- 5,001 of 5,001 exact. Both are cost/scope decisions with a proof path, which is
what these entries now say.
MEASURED ON ONE BC BUILD, EVALUATED ON THREE (eight on main). A difference exists only if the
object carrying it exists on that version AND declares the property shape that produces it, and
BC moves both between minors -- so an entry can be correct on two legs and match nothing on a
third, which the stale-entry check reports as a landed fix. That fired on 27.5 for four
InfopartPageDefinition entries: the only page with a part-control ProviderID is 4306 'Agent
Tasks' on 27.5 and 8705 'Table Information Card' on 28.x, and 27.5's part declares Editable
while 28.x's does not. Deleting them would have broken 27.0 and 28.4, where the differences are
real.
'versionContingent': true exempts an entry from the UNUSED check and from nothing else -- it is
still matched, so it can never hide a difference. 15 of the 117 page entries carry it: every one
whose whole population on the measured build is one or two occurrences, not just the four that
27.5 happened to hit. See docs/metadata-equivalence.md#one-build-measured-three-evaluated.
Measurement caveat: ONE BC build and TWO apps. Base Application's ~4,000 pages are not measured
at all -- apps.json excludes it on COST (257s, 8.83 GiB peak RSS), not because it cannot be
compiled: this line used to say its emit needs a .NET reference no BC artifact ships, which
#3876 disproved -- the reference ships in the ASP.NET Core reference pack and is staged. So
nothing here is evidence about the pages most AL tests actually touch.
The seven pre-existing TranslationKey.* entries already covered the page side without being
touched: they match on member signature, and pages carry the same TranslationKey type.
CodeUnit (#3782 step 2). Measured on BC 28.1.49838.53910 over Business Foundation (25
codeunits) and System Application (533): 2,220 differences across 5 members, all of them
one-directional (BC states a value, the runner states none - the runner invents nothing).
THREE OF THOSE FIVE ARE GONE, landed by #3788, and their entries went with them: ALNamespace,
InherentEntitlements and InherentPermissions. All three were stated by SymbolReference.json and
simply not read - the namespace as the Namespaces TREE PATH an object is reached through (533
of 533 exact against BC's attribute), the two masks as the AL letter spelling in the object's
own Properties bag. The harness measured the result over all 558 codeunits and reported all
three entries STALE, which is what removing them rests on rather than a fixture.
So eight of MetaCodeunit's eleven members now agree EXACTLY across all 558 codeunits: Id, Name,
SubType, TableNo and SingleInstance did already, and those three joined them. What remains is
the two MetaRuntimeInfo entries below - one <Methods> collection counted under two signatures -
and it stays tracked rather than half-landed because it is only PARTLY derivable: BC's emitted
method names are a subset of the symbol file's for 64 codeunits and are NOT for 73, where BC
emits event-publisher and internal methods the symbol file omits.
The two REMAINING CodeUnit entries were AUDITED against versionContingent and neither carries it.
That is a measurement, not an omission: on the three ground-truth bundles present
135/137/138 System Application codeunits. 27.5 is the very leg that reddened step 1, and it
carries them. Step 1's failure was a member whose whole population was ONE page; nothing here is
close. A later step adding a kind should run the same check rather than assume either way.
Query and XmlPort were added to the comparison by #3782 steps 3 and 4, and the 47 entries
below are the result. Measured on BC 28.1.49838.53910 over System Application, the only app
in the bundle set that carries either kind: 7 queries producing 616 differences and 4 xmlports
producing 322. Most of that is already declared by entries neither kind needed to add: the
seven pre-existing TranslationKey.* entries cover 553 of the query total and 24 of the xmlport
one, and step 2's two MetaRuntimeInfo entries cover the remaining 2 -- all of them match on
member SIGNATURE, and every metadata object carries the same TranslationKey and MetaRuntimeInfo
types. So the 47 new entries cover 63 query differences and 296 xmlport ones, 359 in total.
READ THE 47 THE SAME WAY AS THE PAGE ENTRIES: 19 of them are #field / backing-field COMPANION
entries that BC populates from the same value as the member declared beside them. So there
are 28 DISTINCT members, not 47.
issue 3798  12 entries, Query. Nothing structural: every column id, FieldNo, ColumnType,
MethodType, QueryColumnIndex, DataItemLinkType and DataItemTable agrees EXACTLY
on all 7 queries, which is the strongest positive result the harness has
produced for any kind so far. The 12 are 4 properties the symbol file states
(both Inherent masks as 'X', Caption) plus 8 the emitter assigns.
issue 3797  35 entries, XmlPort. 182 of the 322 differences are one finding under two
signatures: all 91 <Node> elements absent, because the runner derives no xmlport
structure at all. Nine further members are computed FROM the nodes and go green
with them; two of those (Schema, SchemaTypeName) do not merely differ but THROW
NullReferenceException on the runner's side, which is #3510's shape.
NONE of these 47 claims a value is UNDERIVABLE, and none claims outOfScope. Four xmlport
properties are stated verbatim in SymbolReference.json and discarded by VisitSymbolContainer,
which keeps TableNo/SingleInstance/Subtype for Codeunit only -- Direction, Encoding and
PreserveWhiteSpace each agree with BC on 3 of 3 where declared. The node tree is the one place
the symbol file genuinely states nothing, and even there the entry says only that the runner
does not derive it today: whether it CAN be reconstructed is unmeasured, and 'nothing is
stored' is evidence about storage, never about derivability.
19 OF THE 47 ARE versionContingent, and which ones is a property of the POPULATION. The 15 page
entries carrying the flag were the ones whose population was one or two occurrences; here the
WHOLE population is 7 queries and 4 xmlports, so the flag goes on every entry whose population
depends on a per-object DECLARATION -- one object gaining or losing it empties the entry, and
the stale check would report that as a landed fix. Direction, Encoding and PreserveWhiteSpace
are stated by 3 of the 4 xmlports; the Inherent masks, APIVersion and CaptionML by 4 of the 7
queries; Permissions, UseRequestForm and the Methods pair by exactly one xmlport each.
THE OTHER 28 DELIBERATELY DO NOT CARRY IT, and that is the more important half. BC writes
those unconditionally for every object of the kind, so their population cannot shrink without
the derivation having changed -- which is exactly what the stale check should report. Applying
the flag to all 49 was tried and MEASURED WRONG: a mutation that made the xmlport projection
state BC's own Direction verbatim -- manufacturing agreement, the precise failure these
entries exist to prevent -- passed all 22 tests, and failed the stale check the moment the
flag came off those two entries. versionContingent exempts an entry from the UNUSED check, so
it cannot hide a difference that EXISTS, but it does hide one that stopped existing for the
wrong reason.
The population stability that would have justified the blanket application is real and is not
sufficient: measured across the four bundles on the authoring box -- 27.5.46862.53931,
(same ids, same property values, same 9/20/22/40 node counts), and the harness runs on
unit-test legs only, which are exactly 27.5 and 28.4.
The two MetaRuntimeInfo entries this step originally carried are GONE: step 2 (#3785) merged
first and its copies survive, which is the resolution both PRs had agreed in writing. They now
cover XmlPort 9864 as well as the codeunits, and their reasons were extended to say so rather
than left stating a codeunit-only population — the xmlport occurrence is closed by #3797, not
by #3788, and the combined population (~146 objects) is why the flag stays off.

SCOPE DECISION BY THE REPOSITORY OWNER, 2026-09-10 (relayed on #3568): translations are out of scope for the runner. In the owner's terms, translations are not relevant right now and nothing in a run has ever had to do with them. So this is a surface the runner does not need to reproduce -- decided, not assumed, and not a statement that the derivation is correct. WHAT THE RUNNER ANSWERS HERE IS UNMEASURED, NOT RIGHT: 0 and Module are what the MetaField ctor's own defaults leave behind, on a surface nothing exercises. Nobody has checked them against BC and nobody should spend effort doing so. Corroborating the decision rather than grounding it: the runner has no .xlf or Translations/ handling anywhere -- zero references in AlRunner/ -- and docs/limitations.md records that it installs no BC translation resources, so no AL test could observe this member today even if the scope call went the other way. Separately measured, and the reason this can never be called a permanent LIMIT: the key IS derivable -- (uint)(FNV-1a-32 over the UTF-16LE bytes of the name + int.MaxValue) reproduces 2,153 of 2,153 keys in the ground truth (TranslationKeysAreDerivable_NotAPermanentLimit). Deriving it is possible and simply not wanted. What invalidates this entry is the owner putting translations back in scope. NOT to be confused with MetaField.CaptionML, which is the caption TEXT, is AL-observable, and is declared separately as a defect.

BC answers AsReadOnly where the runner answers ToBeClassified, on the 5 DECLARED fields whose AL states it. So no AL surface can observe this member, and the runner keeps its own spelling rather than reproducing a spec BC regenerates. The private backing storage behind MetaTable.FieldsById, holding the same merged tableextension fields as MetaTable.Fields.<presence>; same runtime-merged-versus-build-time-emit boundary, same consequence for an empty diff.

The runner models the MERGED RUNTIME state a running system has — every registered app's tableextension fields present on the base table. The ground truth is BC's BUILD-TIME per-app emit, which by construction sees only the app being compiled. Two different things, so this is a limitation of the oracle and not evidence about the runner: 115 fields on four Business Foundation tables (230, 242, 308, 6635). In BC 29 everything is merged at database level anyway, which makes the runner's merged view the forward-looking one. CONSEQUENCE: a multi-app bundle can never produce an empty diff, so a non-empty diff here is expected and must not be read as noise or as a bug. BC's document carries a <Methods> subtree for 145 of the 558 codeunits measured (System Application + Business Foundation, 28.1.49838.53910) and the runner's projection carries none, so every method BC states is reported absent. PARTLY derivable, and the split is MEASURED rather than assumed -- CodeunitMethodTableDerivabilityTests pins each claim below, so this reason cannot quietly stop being true. What BC emits is not the codeunit's methods but its ATTRIBUTED methods: all 326 <Method> elements carry an attribute and 0 carry none, in three kinds. EventPublisherAttribute (169) IS stated by SymbolReference.json, as an IntegrationEvent or InternalEvent method attribute, and is reproduced EXACTLY -- by id, by name and in BC's own order -- for every codeunit BC emits no subscriber for. InherentPermissionsMethodAttribute is stated too, except on the 4 occurrences where the method is local (codeunits 306, 307, 309, 8705). EventSubscriberAttribute (140 in System Application) is stated NOWHERE: the symbol file is an app's consumer-facing API surface, so it carries no `local` method, and an AL event subscriber is always local -- 0 of the 140 appear in it by id OR by name. AN EARLIER VERSION OF THIS REASON HAD THAT BACKWARDS, saying BC emits publisher and internal methods the symbol file omits; the symbol file states the publishers and omits the subscribers, which is a different mechanism with a different remedy, and the 64/73 counts it quoted are the symptom of the wrong comparison rather than of a partial derivation. A PARTIAL SUBTREE IS NOT THE ANSWER, and that is the reason this stays declared rather than half-landed: MetadataObjectDiff pairs Methods POSITIONALLY (it is absent from PairByIdMembers, and MetaMethod spells its id "MethodId", which IdPropertyNames does not list), 10 of the 145 codeunits interleave publishers and subscribers, and no codeunit property separates the 72 codeunits with subscribers from the 461 without -- EventSubscriberInstance appears on 3 of the 72 -- so the runner cannot tell whether its derivation is complete. Modelled over both apps: absence costs 326 one-directional differences, a partial subtree would cost 166 of which 8 would be the runner naming a DIFFERENT method in BC's slot, which is a fabricated association rather than a stated absence. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT is a second input, not a better parse: the runner already reads [NavEventSubscriber] off the loaded R2R assembly (AssemblyTypeIndex.FindAttributedMethods, driven by EventSubscriberPatches), and joining that to the symbol file's publishers supplies both halves. It needs the dependency assembly loaded inside the metadata path, which today reads the .app without loading it. What invalidates this entry is the owner putting translations back in scope. The HelpLink half of #4057 was a real defect and is LANDED, so its two entries are gone rather than reclassified.

Same cause as the ControlDefinition.ID/.Name entries already here (#3926): the differ pairs AllDeltas POSITIONALLY, the render produces no PagePropertiesChange, ExpressionAddDelta, ViewDefinitionAddDelta or ContentChangeDelta, and a document that opens with one therefore pairs every later element one slot early. The object is System Application pageextension 2516 'AppSourceMarketPlaceExtension', whose emitted document is [PagePropertiesChange, ActionAdd, ActionAdd]; the runner renders the two ActionAdds, so BC's AllDeltas[1] pairs against the runner's [1], which is BC's [2]. IT REACHES THE HARNESS ON 27.5 AND NOT ON 28.1, which is why these four members appear later than the 774 ones: 2516 has a deltas document on 27.5 and none on 28.1, so only the 27.5 legs ever compare it (#3923). MEASURED, NOT INFERRED: splicing an empty PagePropertiesChange into the runner's own rendered document -- changing nothing else -- takes 2516 from 6 undeclared differences to 0, and its 222-difference total to 216. So every one of these four is on content the runner renders CORRECTLY. Do not read an ID, Name, ContainerType or OperationType difference here as a wrong value; producing the missing delta kinds removes them. SEPARATELY FIXED in the same change and NOT what these entries cover: the render used to answer ActionItems for 2516's first action, because its AL Anchor is the AREA name 'Navigation' and the render did not recognise it. BC's own CodeAnalysis.Emit.MetadataEmitterHelper.GetContainerType maps ActionAreaKind.Navigation to the runtime container RelatedInformation, and the render now applies that mapping (ExtensionRuntimeDeltasBcMappingTests holds the table to BC's own method). That was a real defect, it is gone, and these four differences survive it.
